c1-4-001.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | It's only ten o'clock, and I ___ three cups of coffee this morning. (drink) |

item.q: It's only ten o'clock, and I ___ three cups of coffee this morning. (drink)
item.why: *this morning* is still going on (it's ten o'clock): present perfect, *I've drunk*.
item.why_lv: *this morning* vēl turpinās (ir *desmit* no rīta): Present Perfect, *I've drunk.*

c1-4-002.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | It's six in the evening now. I ___ much this morning because the internet was down. (not / do) |

item.q: It's six in the evening now. I ___ much this morning because the internet was down. (not / do)
item.why: The morning is over (it's six in the evening): past simple, *I didn't do much this morning*.
item.why_lv: Rīts ir beidzies (ir seši vakarā): Past Simple, *I didn't do much this morning.*

c1-4-003.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: Since she ___ the team, sales have doubled. | joined

wrong: had joined
was joining
joins

item.q: Choose the correct option: Since she ___ the team, sales have doubled.
item.why: *since* + past simple for the point in the past when it started (*since she joined*), present perfect in the main part (*have doubled*).
item.why_lv: *since* + Past Simple brīdim pagātnē, kad tas sākās (*since she joined*), Present Perfect galvenajā daļā (*have doubled*).
wrong: had joined
was joining
joins

c1-4-004.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | Have you made any friends since you ___ in this city? (live) |

item.q: Have you made any friends since you ___ in this city? (live)
item.why: Both situations go on until now (you still live here): present perfect also after *since*: *since you've lived here*.
item.why_lv: *Abas* situācijas turpinās līdz šim brīdim (*tu* joprojām *te* dzīvo): Present Perfect arī aiz *since*: *since you've lived here*.

c1-4-005.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | I'll text you the moment I ___ my exam results. (get) |

item.q: I'll text you the moment I ___ my exam results. (get)
item.why: *the moment* about the future: present perfect (*the moment I've got my results*) or present simple, never *will* or the past.
item.why_lv: *the moment* par nākotni: Present Perfect (*the moment I've got my results*) vai Present Simple, nevis *will* vai pagātne.

c1-4-006.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Once you paid, the order can't be changed.

key.correct: Once you paid, the order can't be changed.
wrong: The moment we landed, I texted her.
After she had left hospital, she went on a long holiday.
I'll call you as soon as I've finished.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: *Once* about something that has not happened yet (*the order can't be changed*): present perfect or present simple, *Once you've paid*. *The moment we landed* is about the past, so the past simple is right there.
item.why_lv: *Once* par to, kas vēl nav *noticis* (*the order can't be changed*): Present Perfect vai Present Simple, *Once you've paid.* *The moment we landed* ir par pagātni, tāpēc tur Past Simple ir *pareizi*.
item.correct: Once you paid, the order can't be changed.
wrong: The moment we landed, I texted her.
After she had left hospital, she went on a long holiday.
I'll call you as soon as I've finished.

c1-4-007.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | This is the third time she ___ her keys this week! (lose) |

item.q: This is the third time she ___ her keys this week! (lose)
item.why: *This is the first / second / third time* + present perfect: *she has lost her keys*.
item.why_lv: *This is the first / second / third time* + Present Perfect: *she has lost her keys*.

c1-4-008.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | This is the first time I am seeing snow.

key.correct: This is the first time I am seeing snow.
wrong: It was the first time I'd been on a plane.
It's the second time he has missed the train this month.
It won't be the first time they've voted against the plan.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: After *This is the first time*, the present perfect: *This is the first time I've seen snow.* After *It was the first time*, the past perfect.
item.why_lv: Aiz *This is the first time* lieto Present Perfect: *This is the first time I've seen snow.* Aiz *It was the first time* lieto Past Perfect.
item.correct: This is the first time I am seeing snow.
wrong: It was the first time I'd been on a plane.
It's the second time he has missed the train this month.
It won't be the first time they've voted against the plan.

c1-4-009.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | It's only eleven, and I ___ the bank four times. Nobody answers. (ring) |

item.q: It's only eleven, and I ___ the bank four times. Nobody answers. (ring)
item.why: A number of times (*four times*): present perfect simple, *I've rung*. The continuous is for the activity: *I've been ringing all morning*.
item.why_lv: Reižu *skaits* (*four times*): Present Perfect Simple, *I've rung.* Continuous forma ir darbībai: *I've been ringing all morning.*

c1-4-010.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I've been having this phone since May.

key.correct: I've been having this phone since May.
wrong: Rents have gone up by eight per cent this year.
She's been learning Spanish for two years.
I've been ringing the bank all morning.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: *have* meaning *own* is a state: present perfect simple, *I've had this phone since May*.
item.why_lv: *have* nozīmē piederēt ir stāvoklis: Present Perfect Simple, *I've had this phone since May.*
item.correct: I've been having this phone since May.
wrong: Rents have gone up by eight per cent this year.
She's been learning Spanish for two years.
I've been ringing the bank all morning.

c1-4-011.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | By next May I ___ at this school for ten years. (teach) |

item.q: By next May I ___ at this school for ten years. (teach)
item.why: Up to a point in the future (*by next May*): future perfect, *I'll have taught* or *I'll have been teaching*.
item.why_lv: Līdz brīdim nākotnē (*by next May*): Future Perfect, *I'll have taught* vai *I'll have been teaching.*

c1-4-012.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | gap | The thief is thought ___ the country last week. (leave) |

item.q: The thief is thought ___ the country last week. (leave)
item.why: *is thought* is now, the leaving was earlier (*last week*): the perfect after *to*, *to have left*.
item.why_lv: *is thought* ir tagad, aizbraukšana bija agrāk (*last week*): *perfekts* aiz to, *to have left*.

c1-4-013.gate_key: adv_perfect | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: She denied ___ the letter. | having read

wrong: to have read
have read
to read

item.q: Choose the correct option: She denied ___ the letter.
item.why: *deny* is followed by an *-ing* form; for something earlier, *having* + past participle: *She denied having read the letter* (*denied reading* is also correct).
item.why_lv: Aiz *deny* lieto *-ing* formu; par kaut ko agrāku *having* + 3. forma: *She denied having read the letter* (*pareizi* arī *denied reading*).
wrong: to have read
have read
to read

c1-4-014.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Last night he would cook dinner for all of us.

key.correct: Last night he would cook dinner for all of us.
wrong: Our cat will sit at the window for hours.
At school she would always sit at the back.
Wood will float on water.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: *will / would* describe typical behaviour, not one occasion: *Last night he cooked dinner for all of us.*
item.why_lv: *will / would* apraksta raksturīgu uzvedību, nevis vienu *reizi*: *Last night he cooked dinner for all of us.*
item.correct: Last night he would cook dinner for all of us.
wrong: Our cat will sit at the window for hours.
At school she would always sit at the back.
Wood will float on water.

c1-4-015.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | The old factory would be next to the river.

key.correct: The old factory would be next to the river.
wrong: Whenever we visited my uncle, we would play in his garden.
Didn't you use to have red hair?
We visited Switzerland four times in the nineties.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: For a past state that has changed, use *used to*, not *would*: *The old factory used to be next to the river.*
item.why_lv: Pagātnes stāvoklim, kas mainījies, lieto *used to*, nevis *would*: *The old factory used to be next to the river.*
item.correct: The old factory would be next to the river.
wrong: Whenever we visited my uncle, we would play in his garden.
Didn't you use to have red hair?
We visited Switzerland four times in the nineties.

c1-4-016.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | gap | I tried three times, but the printer ___ work this morning. (not / will) |

item.q: I tried three times, but the printer ___ work this morning. (not / will)
item.why: *wouldn't* for a refusal on one occasion, also by a thing: *the printer wouldn't work*.
item.why_lv: *wouldn't atteikumam* vienā reizē, arī *lietai*: *the printer wouldn't work*.

c1-4-017.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | gap | "I've got a headache." "Well, if you ___ stare at a screen all day, what do you expect?" |

item.q: "I've got a headache." "Well, if you ___ stare at a screen all day, what do you expect?"
item.why: *if you will* + verb criticises something the person keeps doing: *if you will stare at a screen all day*.
item.why_lv: *if you will* + darbības vārds kritizē to, ko cilvēks dara *atkal* un *atkal*: *if you will stare at a screen all day*.

c1-4-018.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | gap | Don't ring them now: they ___ lunch. (will / have) |

item.q: Don't ring them now: they ___ lunch. (will / have)
item.why: A confident guess about what is happening now: *will be* + *-ing*, *they'll be having lunch*.
item.why_lv: Drošs minējums par to, kas notiek tagad: *will be + -ing, they'll be having lunch*.

c1-4-019.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | gap | It's nine o'clock. She ___ the news by now. (will / hear) |

item.q: It's nine o'clock. She ___ the news by now. (will / hear)
item.why: A confident guess about something before now: *will have* + past participle, *she'll have heard the news by now*.
item.why_lv: Drošs minējums par to, kas jau *noticis*: *will have* + 3. forma, *she'll have heard the news by now*.

c1-4-020.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | gap | I ___ to your party, but nobody told me about it. (come) |

item.q: I ___ to your party, but nobody told me about it. (come)
item.why: Something that did not happen in the past: *would have* + past participle, *I'd have come*.
item.why_lv: Kaut kas, kas pagātnē nenotika: *would have* + 3. forma, *I'd have come.*

c1-4-021.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | gap | I sent it on Monday, so the parcel ___ by now. (should / arrive) |

item.q: I sent it on Monday, so the parcel ___ by now. (should / arrive)
item.why: *should have* + past participle for what we expect has happened: *the parcel should have arrived by now*.
item.why_lv: *should have* + 3. forma tam, ko sagaidām, ka jau ir *noticis*: *the parcel should have arrived by now*.

c1-4-022.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Should you will change your mind, just call us.

key.correct: Should you will change your mind, just call us.
wrong: If you will follow me, I'll show you to your room.
If you should need anything, just ask.
If you'd take a seat, the doctor will see you shortly.

item.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
item.why: *Should you* + base verb (= if you happen to): *Should you change your mind, just call us.* *If you will / would* = if you are willing.
item.why_lv: *Should you* + pamatforma (= ja gadījumā): *Should you change your mind, just call us.* *If you will / would* = ja *esat* ar *mieru*.
item.correct: Should you will change your mind, just call us.
wrong: If you will follow me, I'll show you to your room.
If you should need anything, just ask.
If you'd take a seat, the doctor will see you shortly.

c1-4-023.gate_key: adv_will | C1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: Keep the receipt in case you ___ to return the shoes. | should need

wrong: will need
would need
should to need

item.q: Choose the correct option: Keep the receipt in case you ___ to return the shoes.
item.why: *in case* + *should* (or the present simple) for a small chance: *in case you should need to return them*, not *will*.
item.why_lv: *in case + should* (vai Present Simple) *nelielai* iespējai: *in case you should need to return them*, nevis *will*.
wrong: will need
would need
should to need
